zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat Fuṣṣilat
﷽
﴿حم﴾ ﴿تَنْـزِيلٌ مِنَ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 2] — "تَنْزِيلٌ" is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿كِتابٌ فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3]; this is the view of the Basrans. Al-Farrāʾ said: it is permissible that "تَنْزِيلٌ" be made nominative by "حـم", and it is permissible that it be nominative by implying "هَذا", the meaning being: "This is a revelation from the Mighty, the Merciful", that is: "It is a revelation". ﴿قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3] — "قُرْآنًا" is made accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "its verses have been made clear as a Quran", that is: "its verses have been made clear in the state of its being gathered as Arabic". ﴿لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 3], that is: We have made it clear for whoever knows.
﴿بَشِيرًا ونَذِيرًا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 4] are among its attributes.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿وَبارَكَ فِيها وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾ — on Tuesday and Wednesday, so the total became four days. That is His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ فِيها رَواسِيَ مِن فَوْقِها وبارَكَ فِيها وقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها في أرْبَعَةِ أيّامٍ﴾, that is: in the completion of four days. ﴿سَواءً لِلسّائِلِينَ﴾ — and "سَواءٍ"; the nominative is also permissible. Whoever reads the genitive makes it an attribute of the days, the meaning being: "in four equal days". Whoever reads the accusative takes it as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "they were equal, equally (سَواءً، واسْتِواءً)". Whoever reads the nominative takes it in the sense: "they are equal". And "لِلسّائِلِينَ" is attached to His saying: ﴿وَقَدَّرَ فِيها أقْواتَها﴾ — for everyone in need of sustenance; it was said "لِلسّائِلِينَ" (for those who ask) only because everyone seeks sustenance and asks for it. It is also possible that "لِلسّائِلِينَ" means: for whoever asked "In how many [days] were the heavens and the earths created?", so it was said: "The earth was created in four equal days, with no addition and no shortfall", as an answer to whoever asked.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿ثُمَّ اسْتَوى إلى السَّماءِ وهي دُخانٌ فَقالَ لَها ولِلأرْضِ﴾ (the verse) — the meaning of "اسْتَوى" is: He turned to the heaven and directed [His will]. ﴿قالَتا أتَيْنا طائِعِينَ﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). It was said "طائِعِينَ" rather than "طائِعاتٍ" only because they were treated like beings that reason and discern, as it was said of the stars: ﴿وَكُلٌّ في فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾ [Yā Sīn: 40]. It has also been said: "they said: we come — that is, we and whoever is in us — willingly". And the meaning of "طَوْعًا أوْ كَرْهًا" is in the sense: "obey what I have commanded willingly", in the position of "obey with obedience, or be compelled with compulsion".

zajjaj:12-12.t:
﴿فَقَضاهُنَّ﴾: He created them and made them. Abū Dhuʾayb said:
وَعَلَيْهِما مَسْرُودَتانِ قَضاهُما ∗∗∗ داوُدُ أوْ صَنَعَ السَّوابِغَ تُبَّعُ
(Upon the two of them are two coats of linked mail which David made, or Tubbaʿ fashioned the ample [mail].)
Its meaning is: "he worked them and made them". ﴿وَأوْحى في كُلِّ سَماءٍ أمْرَها﴾ — it was said: "what sets it right", and it was said: "its angels". ﴿وَزَيَّنّا السَّماءَ الدُّنْيا بِمَصابِيحَ وحِفْظًا﴾ — its meaning is: "and We guarded it with the stars from the eavesdropping of the devils, a guarding". So He said: say, do you disbelieve in the One whose power is this, and assign rivals to Him — that is, idols which you carve with your own hands? ﴿ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ العَزِيزِ العَلِيمِ﴾, that is: the One whose attribute this is, and who has this power, the Lord of the worlds.

zajjaj:13-13.t: Then He said: ﴿فَإنْ أعْرَضُوا﴾, that is: if they do not accept your message after this clarification and affirm the oneness of Allah, ﴿فَقُلْ أنْذَرْتُكم صاعِقَةً مِثْلَ صاعِقَةِ عادٍ وثَمُودَ﴾, that is: I have warned you that there will befall you what befell those nations before you that disbelieved.

zajjaj:15-15.t: Then He related the story of their disbelief and the cause of their insolence and their persistence in their misguidance, saying: ﴿فَأمّا عادٌ فاسْتَكْبَرُوا في الأرْضِ بِغَيْرِ الحَقِّ وقالُوا مَن أشَدُّ مِنّا قُوَّةً﴾. So Allah sent upon them a furious wind, and He said: ﴿فَأرْسَلْنا عَلَيْهِمْ رِيحًا صَرْصَرًا في أيّامٍ نَحِساتٍ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 16] — and "نَحْساتٍ" is also transmitted. Abū ʿUbayda said: "الصَّرْصَر" is the one with a violent sound, and it has come in the commentary: the intensely cold one. "نَحِساتٍ" means ill-omened; its singular is "نَحِسٌ"; and whoever reads "نَحْساتٍ", its singular is "نَحْسٌ". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿فِي يَوْمِ نَحْسٍ مُسْتَمِرٍّ﴾ [al-Qamar: 19]

zajjaj:17-17.t:
﴿وَأمّا ثَمُودُ فَهَدَيْناهُمْ﴾ — the good [reading] is dropping the tanwīn. It is read "ثَمُودٌ" with tanwīn, and "ثَمُودًا" in the accusative is permissible, by an implied verb which the overt one explains. As for the meaning of "هَدَيْناهم", Qatāda said: "We made clear to them the path of guidance and the path of misguidance." ﴿فاسْتَحَبُّوا العَمى عَلى الهُدى﴾. The preferred choice is the nominative of "ثَمُودُ", as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); this is the view of all the grammarians — preferring the nominative — and all of them allow the accusative.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأخَذَتْهم صاعِقَةُ العَذابِ الهُونِ﴾ — "الهُون" is the abasement and disgrace which humiliates them and disgraces them.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
﴿وَيَوْمَ يُحْشَرُ أعْداءُ اللَّهِ إلى النّارِ فَهم يُوزَعُونَ﴾ — "إلى النّارِ" is read with fatḥa on the nūn and full (tafkhīm) pronunciation, and the reading of Abū ʿAmr is "إلى النِّارِ" with imāla (inclination) towards kasra. He prefers that — meaning the kasra — only with the rāʾ, because it is a letter with repetition (takrīr) in it; for that reason Abū ʿAmr preferred the kasra. ﴿فَهم يُوزَعُونَ﴾ — it has come in the commentary: "the first of them are held back for the last of them". Its origin is from "وَزَعْتُهُ", when you restrain him. Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said when he took up the judgeship: "People must have restrainers (وَزَعَة)", that is: they must have helpers who restrain people from transgression.
﴿شَهِدَ عَلَيْهِمْ سَمْعُهم وأبْصارُهم وجُلُودُهُمْ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 20] — it has come in the commentary that "جُلُودُهم" (their skins) is a euphemism for the private parts; the meaning is: their private parts will testify to their sins.

zajjaj:21-21.t: ﴿وَقالُوا لِجُلُودِهِمْ لِمَ شَهِدْتُمْ عَلَيْنا قالُوا أنْطَقَنا اللَّهُ﴾, that is: Allah made us witnesses.

zajjaj:23-23.t: ﴿وَذَلِكم ظَنُّكُمُ﴾ — it is nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and "أرْداكم" is a second khabar. It is also permissible that "ظَنُّكُمُ" be a badal (substitute) for "ذَلِكم", the meaning being: "and your thought which you thought about your Lord has ruined you". The meaning of "أرْداكم" is: it has destroyed you.

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿وَقَيَّضْنا﴾: "and We arranged", from where they did not reckon, ﴿لَهم قُرَناءَ﴾ (the verse). He is saying: they made attractive to them their deeds which they do and witness, and what is behind them, and what they resolve to do.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لا تَسْمَعُوا لِهَذا القُرْآنِ والغَوْا فِيهِ﴾, that is: oppose it with speech that is not understood, that speech being idle talk (لَغْو). One says: "لَغا، يَلْغُو، لَغْوًا", and one says: "لَغِيَ، يَلْغى، لَغْوًا", when one speaks idle talk, which is speech that yields nothing and whose reality you do not understand.

zajjaj:28-28.t:
﴿ذَلِكَ جَزاءُ أعْداءِ اللَّهِ النّارُ﴾ — what indicates its nominative is His saying: ﴿فَلَنُذِيقَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا عَذابًا شَدِيدًا﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 27]; the meaning is: "that severe punishment is the recompense of the enemies of Allah". "النّار" is nominative, a badal (substitute) for "جَزاءُ أعْداءِ اللَّهِ". If you wish, you may make "النّار" nominative as an explanation, as though it were said: "What is it?" and it was said: "It is the Fire". ﴿لَهم فِيها دارُ الخُلْدِ﴾, that is: they have in the Fire the abode of eternity, and the Fire is the abode itself, just as you say: "you have in this house a house of joy", while you mean the house itself. As the poet said:
أخُو رَغائِبَ يُعْطِيها ويَسْألُها ∗∗∗ يَأْبى الظُّلامَةَ مِنهُ النَّوْفَلُ الزُّفَرُ
(A man of great desires, who gives them and asks for them; from him the generous, burden-bearing one refuses injustice.)

zajjaj:29-29.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا رَبَّنا أرِنا﴾ — with kasra on the rāʾ, and with it made quiescent because of the heaviness of the kasra, as they said "فَخْذٌ" for "فَخِذٌ" (thigh). Whoever gives it kasra follows the original, and the kasra is better, because originally it is "أرْئِنا": the hamza was dropped and the kasra remained as an indication of it; and the kasra is better. The meaning of the verse, according to what has come in the commentary, is that by the two He means the son of Adam, Qābīl, who killed his brother, and Iblīs: Qābīl is of mankind and Iblīs is of the jinn. And the meaning of ﴿نَجْعَلْهُما تَحْتَ أقْدامِنا﴾ is: that they be in the lowest depth.

zajjaj:30-30.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ قالُوا رَبُّنا اللَّهُ ثُمَّ اسْتَقامُوا﴾, that is: they affirmed the oneness of Allah and were steadfast, acted in obedience to Him and kept to the sunna of His Prophet. ﴿تَتَنَـزَّلُ عَلَيْهِمُ المَلائِكَةُ﴾ as bearers of good news, giving them good news at death and at the time of resurrection, so that the terrors of the Resurrection do not alarm them.

zajjaj:32-32.t: His saying: ﴿نُـزُلا مِن غَفُورٍ رَحِيمٍ﴾ — its meaning is: and rejoice in the Garden, in which you will be lodged as a hospitable lodging. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said: "نُزُلًا" is accusative in two ways. One of them is that it be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), in the sense: "you will have in it whatever your souls desire; We have lodged it as a lodging". It is also permissible that it be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), in the sense: "you will have in it whatever your souls desire, as a lodging", just as you say: "جاءَ زَيْدٌ مَشْيًا" (Zayd came walking), in the sense of "جاءَ زَيْدٌ ماشِيًا".

zajjaj:33-33.t: ﴿وَمَن أحْسَنُ قَوْلا﴾ — [قَوْلًا] is accusative as an explanation (tafsīr, i.e. tamyīz), just as you say: "زَيْدٌ أحْسَنُ مِنكَ وجْهًا" (Zayd is more handsome than you in face). It has come in the commentary that Muḥammad ﷺ is meant by it, because he called to the oneness of Allah. And it has also come in the commentary from ʿĀʾisha and others that it was revealed about the muezzins.

zajjaj:34-34.t: ﴿وَلا تَسْتَوِي الحَسَنَةُ ولا السَّيِّئَةُ﴾ — "لا" is redundant (zāʾida) and emphatic; the meaning is: "the good deed and the evil deed are not equal". ﴿ادْفَعْ بِالَّتِي هي أحْسَنُ﴾ — its meaning is: "repel the evil deed with that which is better". ﴿كَأنَّهُ ولِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ﴾ — "الحَمِيم" is the near relative.

zajjaj:35-35.t: ﴿وَما يُلَقّاها إلا الَّذِينَ صَبَرُوا﴾, that is: none is granted the reward of this — that is, none is granted this deed — except those who are patient, that is: except those who restrain anger. ﴿وَما يُلَقّاها إلا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — "الحَظّ" here is the Garden, that is: none is granted it except one for whom the Garden has become due. And the meaning of "ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمٍ" is: "a great share in good".

zajjaj:36-36.t: ﴿وَإمّا يَنْـزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَـزْغٌ﴾ — He is saying: if there comes to you from Satan an incitement by which he turns you away from forbearance, seek refuge in Allah from his evil and continue in your forbearance.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ اللَّيْلُ والنَّهارُ﴾, that is: among His signs which indicate that He is One.
And His saying: ﴿واسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾ — He has said "the night, the day and the moon", which are masculine, and He said "خَلَقَهُنَّ", and the hāʾ and nūn indicate the feminine. There are two aspects to it. One of them is that the pronoun for what does not reason follows the form of the feminine: you say "هَذِهِ كِباشُكَ فَسُقْها" (these are your rams, so drive them [fem. sing.]), and if you wish, "فَسُقْهُنَّ" [fem. pl.]; "خَلَقَهم" [masc. pl.] would only be for what reasons, nothing else. It is also permissible that "خَلَقَهُنَّ" refer back to the meaning of "the signs", because He said: "and among His signs are these things", ﴿واسْجُدُوا لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَهُنَّ﴾

zajjaj:38-38.t: ﴿فَإنِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا فالَّذِينَ عِنْدَ رَبِّكَ﴾ — this is an address to Muḥammad ﷺ, and "الَّذِينَ" here means the angels. So the meaning is: "if they are arrogant and do not affirm the oneness of Allah, worship Him and believe in His Messenger, then the angels glorify Him by night and day". ﴿وَهم لا يَسْأمُونَ﴾: they do not weary.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
Then He added to the proof for them, saying: ﴿وَمِن آياتِهِ أنَّكَ تَرى الأرْضَ خاشِعَةً﴾, that is: crumbled and changed; it is like "هامِدَةً" (barren).
﴿فَإذا أنْـزَلْنا عَلَيْها الماءَ اهْتَزَّتْ ورَبَتْ﴾ — and it is read "وَرَبَأتْ" with hamza. The meaning of "رَبَتْ" is: it swelled, and the meaning of "رَبَأتْ" is: it rose, because when a plant is about to appear the earth rises for it.

zajjaj:40-40.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُلْحِدُونَ في آياتِنا لا يَخْفَوْنَ عَلَيْنا﴾ — and "يَلْحَدُونَ" with fatḥa on the yāʾ and the ḥāʾ. The explanation of "يَلْحَدُونَ" is: they put speech in other than its proper direction. From this is "اللَّحْد" (the niche-grave), because it is the digging in the side of the grave. One says "لَحَدَ" and "ألْحَدَ" with one meaning. ﴿اعْمَلُوا ما شِئْتُمْ﴾ — the wording of this speech is the wording of a command, and its meaning is threat and menace; He has already made clear to them the requital for good and evil.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَكِتابٌ عَزِيزٌ﴾ ﴿لا يَأْتِيهِ الباطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ ولا مِن خَلْفِهِ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 42] — there are two aspects to it. One of them is that the books which preceded do not nullify it, and no book comes after it to nullify it. The second aspect is that it is guarded against anything being taken away from it, so that falsehood would come to it from before it, or anything being added to it, so that falsehood would come to it from behind it. The proof of this is His saying: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نَـزَّلْنا الذِّكْرَ وإنّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 9]

zajjaj:43-43.t: ﴿ما يُقالُ لَكَ إلا ما قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبْلِكَ﴾, that is: you are denied as the messengers before you were denied, and it was said to them just as the disbelievers say to you. Then He said: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّكَ لَذُو مَغْفِرَةٍ﴾ — the meaning is: for whoever believes in you; ﴿وَذُو عِقابٍ ألِيمٍ﴾ for whoever denies you.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا أعْجَمِيًّا لَقالُوا لَوْلا فُصِّلَتْ آياتُهُ﴾, that is: made clear. ﴿أأعْجَمِيٌّ وعَرَبِيٌّ﴾ — it is read "أأعْجَمِيٌّ" with two hamzas, and "أعْجَمِيٌّ" with one hamza, and with a hamza followed by a lightened one that resembles alif; it is not permissible for it to be a pure alif, because after it comes the ʿayn, which is quiescent. It is also read "أعَجَمِيٌّ وعَرَبِيٌّ" with one hamza and fatḥa on the ʿayn. Al-Ḥasan read "أعْجَمِيٌّ" with a hamza and a quiescent ʿayn. What has come in the commentary is that the meaning is: "Had We made it a non-Arabic Quran, they would have said: Why — why not — have its verses been made clear? A non-Arabic Quran and an Arab prophet?!" Whoever reads "آعْجَمِيٌّ", with hamza and alif, [takes it as] a relative adjective (nisba) attributed to the non-Arabic tongue (al-aʿjam). You say "هَذا رَجُلٌ أعْجَمِيٌّ" when he does not speak clearly, whether he is of the non-Arabs or of the Arabs; and you say "هَذا رَجُلٌ عَجَمِيٌّ" when he is of the non-Arabs, whether he speaks clearly or not. Similar to that is "هَذا رَجُلٌ أعْرابِيٌّ" (a Bedouin man), when he is of the people of the desert, whether his stock is Arab or non-Arab. The best in the Quran is "آعْجَمِيٌّ", with hamza and alif, by way of attribution to al-aʿjam. Do you not see His saying: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا أعْجَمِيًّا﴾, and no one read "عَجَمِيًّا"? As for the reading of al-Ḥasan — I mean "أعْجَمِيٌّ" with the ʿayn quiescent — it is not in the sense of a question, but in the sense of "why have its verses not been made clear", so that part of it would be a clarification for the non-Arabs and part of it a clarification for the Arabs. All of these four aspects are acceptable in Arabic, and its commentary goes accordingly.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ هو لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا هُدًى وشِفاءٌ﴾, meaning the Quran; ﴿والَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ في آذانِهِمْ وقْرٌ﴾, that is: in refusing to accept, they are in the position of one who has deafness in his ear. ﴿وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِمْ عَمًى﴾ — and it is read "وَهو عَلَيْهِمْ عَمٍ" with kasra on the mīm and tanwīn; "وَهو عَلَيْهِمْ عَمِيَ" with the yāʾ retained and given fatḥa is also permissible, but it is not permissible to make the yāʾ quiescent and drop the tanwīn. ﴿أُولَئِكَ يُنادَوْنَ مِن مَكانٍ بَعِيدٍ﴾, meaning that, because of the hardness of their hearts, what is recited to them is far removed from them.

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِن رَبِّكَ﴾ — the word is: their being promised the Hour. He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿بَلِ السّاعَةُ مَوْعِدُهُمْ﴾ [al-Qamar: 46]

zajjaj:46-46.t: ﴿وَمَن أساءَ فَعَلَيْها﴾, that is: against himself. And what indicates that the word here is the Hour

zajjaj:47-47.t:
is His saying: ﴿إلَيْهِ يُرَدُّ عِلْمُ السّاعَةِ﴾.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما تَخْرُجُ مِن ثَمَراتٍ مِن أكْمامِها﴾ — like the emergence of the palm spathe from its husk. ﴿وَيَوْمَ يُنادِيهِمْ أيْنَ شُرَكائِي﴾ — the meaning is: "Where is your saying that I have partners?!", and Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, is One, having no partner. He has made that clear in His saying: ﴿أيْنَ شُرَكائِي قالُوا آذَنّاكَ ما مِنّا مِن شَهِيدٍ﴾ — "آذَنّاكَ": we have informed You; there is none among us who bears witness for them.

zajjaj:48-48.t: ﴿وَظَنُّوا ما لَهم مِن مَحِيصٍ﴾, that is: they were certain.

zajjaj:49-49.t: ﴿لا يَسْأمُ الإنْسانُ مِن دُعاءِ الخَيْرِ﴾: he does not weary of the good that befalls him, and when he is tested with something of evil he despairs and loses hope.

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالُوا قُلُوبُنا في أكِنَّةٍ﴾ — "in coverings", that is: "what you call us to does not reach our hearts, because they are in coverings". The singular of "الأكِنَّة" is "كِنان". ﴿وَفِي آذانِنا وقْرٌ﴾, that is: deafness, and a lock which prevents listening to your speech; that is: in refusing to accept from you we are in the position of one who does not hear your speech. ﴿وَمِن بَيْنِنا وبَيْنِكَ حِجابٌ﴾, that is: a barrier in creed and religion. It is like "قُلُوبُنا في أكِنَّةٍ", except that the meaning of this is that we do not join with you in any doctrine. ﴿فاعْمَلْ إنَّنا عامِلُونَ﴾, that is: [we are working] according to our doctrine, and you are working according to your doctrine. It may also be: "work at nullifying our doctrine; we are working at nullifying your cause".

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أذَقْناهُ رَحْمَةً مِنّا مِن بَعْدِ ضَرّاءَ مَسَّتْهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هَذا لِي﴾, that is: this is due to me; I have earned it by my work. The disbelievers are meant by this, and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿وَما أظُنُّ السّاعَةَ قائِمَةً ولَئِنْ رُجِعْتُ إلى رَبِّي إنَّ لِي عِنْدَهُ لَلْحُسْنى﴾. He is saying: I am not certain of the resurrection and the coming of the Hour; but if the matter is so, then I will have with Him the best.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿وَإذا أنْعَمْنا عَلى الإنْسانِ أعْرَضَ ونَأى بِجانِبِهِ﴾ — and it is read "ناءَ", and the meaning is close. He is saying: when he is in blessing, he distances himself from remembering Allah and calling on Him. ﴿وَإذا مَسَّهُ الشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعاءٍ عَرِيضٍ﴾ — "عَرِيضٍ" here means: great; and likewise if it were "ذُو دُعاءٍ طَوِيلٍ" (of long supplication), its meaning would be: "great".

zajjaj:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿سَنُرِيهِمْ آياتِنا في الآفاقِ وفي أنْفُسِهِمْ﴾, that is: We will show them the landmarks which indicate the oneness [of Allah] in the horizons — its singular is "أُفُق". He is saying: We will show them the traces of those who passed before them among the nations that denied the messengers, and the traces of Allah's creation in all lands; and in themselves: that they were drops of semen, then clots, then lumps of flesh, then bones clothed with flesh, then they were brought on to discernment and reason. All of that is proof that the One who did it is One, there is nothing like Him. ﴿أوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أنَّهُ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾ — "إنَّهُ" is also permissible, but the reading is "أنَّهُ" with fatḥa. The position of "بِرَبِّكَ" is nominative in meaning; the meaning is: "Is your Lord not sufficient...?!" The position of "أنَّهُ" is accusative, or if you wish it is nominative. The meaning with the accusative is: "Is your Lord not sufficient in that He is Witness over all things?" And whoever takes it as nominative does so as a badal (substitute); the meaning is: "Is it not sufficient that your Lord is Witness over all things?", that is: "Does the testimony of your Lord not suffice them?!" The meaning of sufficiency here is that He has made clear to them what suffices as proof of His oneness, and His messengers have made it clear.

zajjaj:54-54.t: ﴿ألا إنَّهم في مِرْيَةٍ مِن لِقاءِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾: in doubt. "ألا" is a word with which [speech] is begun; the one addressed is alerted by it, as an emphasis indicating the soundness of what follows it. ﴿ألا إنَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُحِيطٌ﴾, that is: Knower of all things, with a knowledge that encompasses what is manifest and what is hidden.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿وَوَيْلٌ لِلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾ ﴿الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْتُونَ الزَّكاةَ﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 7], that is: they do not consider it obligatory upon them, and they do not give it.

zajjaj:9-9.t: ﴿قُلْ أإنَّكم لَتَكْفُرُونَ بِالَّذِي خَلَقَ الأرْضَ في يَوْمَيْنِ﴾ — had He, Majestic and Exalted is He, willed to create it in an instant, He would have done so, and that would have been well within His power; but He loved that creation should see the aspects of deliberateness, and of power to create the heavens and the earth in many days and in a single instant, because all created beings and the angels brought near, if they gathered together to create the weight of a speck of it, would not create it. And it has come in the commentary that the beginning of the creation of the earth was on Sunday, and its creation was completed on Monday.
